Pulled only the single patient's administrative, quasi-identifier, direct-identifier and clinical fields needed to compose a care-team summary (diagnoses, meds, allergies, labs/imaging, encounter/admission context); excluded contact and financial fields as unnecessary/impermissible under the care_coordination policy, applied PSEUDO-EXPORT to direct identifiers, capped retention at the 90-day ceiling with PURGE-01 deletion, and relied on TLS/ENC-REST/ACL-STORE safeguards with AUDIT-LOG and ROPA for accountability under the LU-CARE legitimate-use basis.

samples.rationale: For ward-level care coordination we pull only the identifiers and administrative timestamps needed to show who is currently on each ward and when they were last seen (admission record plus most recent clinical encounter), across all current patients rather than a single subject; direct identifiers are pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT) per policy, retention is capped at the 90-day ceiling with scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), transport/at-rest encryption and RBAC are in place (TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE), the run is logged (AUDIT-LOG) and recorded in the ROPA under the DPO's accountability, and processing rests on the legitimate-use basis for which the patient provided her data (LU-CARE), covered by the registration-time notice (NOTICE-REG-2026).

Only the clinical fields needed to cross-check current medication against diagnosis and allergies for the named patient (scope=subject) are pulled, keeping the MRN as the sole direct identifier for linkage; it will be pseudonymised on export per policy. Care coordination is a recognised legitimate use (LU-CARE) covered by the registration-time notice, retained up to the 90-day policy ceiling with scheduled audited purge, and protected by TLS, at-rest encryption, RBAC, audit logging, DPO accountability, and ROPA record-keeping, with no onward/secondary use.

Only clinical fields (diagnosis, medication, allergy) plus the mrn needed to identify the single named patient are pulled from clinical_ehr, satisfying data minimisation for a medication-vs-diagnosis-vs-allergy review; the direct identifier (mrn) is pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT) per the care-coordination policy, with TLS/ENC-REST/ACL-STORE safeguards, LU-CARE as the recorded legitimate-use basis, PURGE-01 deletion at the 90-day ceiling, and AUDIT-LOG/ROPA/DPO for accountability.

Only the clinical fields needed to cross-check current medication against diagnosis and allergies for a single named patient were selected (mrn for linkage/pseudonymisation, diagnosis, medication, allergy, and encounter_datetime to establish recency); demographic, financial, and ancillary fields were excluded as unnecessary for this purpose under data minimisation. Direct identifiers are pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT), transport/storage are encrypted and access-controlled (TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE), retention is capped well within the 90-day policy ceiling with scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), processing rests on the legitimate-use basis for provision of medical services (LU-CARE) covered by the registration-time notice (NOTICE-REG-2026), and the run is logged (AUDIT-LOG), accountable to the DPO, and recorded in the ROPA.

Only the minimal patient_administration fields needed to identify and contact patients about their scheduled appointment (mrn, name, phone, email, appointment/admission datetime) are fetched, scoped to all patients with upcoming appointments; pseudonymisation is skipped because direct contact details are required to deliver the reminder, and all technical/organisational controls available in this deployment (TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, PURGE-01, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA, DPO accountability, and the registration notice) are applied under the registration/scheduling legitimate-use basis (LU-REG), with retention capped well below the 180-day ceiling since the purpose ends once the appointment has passed.

Only contact and administrative fields needed to identify patients and notify them of their scheduled appointment time are fetched, consistent with the registration/scheduling purpose under legitimate use LU-REG; direct identifiers (MRN, name, phone) are required unpseudonymised to route the reminder, while quasi-identifiers and clinical/financial data are excluded per data minimisation. Retention is capped well below the 180-day ceiling since the reminder purpose lapses shortly after the appointment, with TLS/ENC-REST/ACL-STORE safeguards, PURGE-01 deletion, AUDIT-LOG logging, DPO accountability, and ROPA record-keeping in place.

Only the minimal identifier and contact fields (mrn, name, phone, email) plus the scheduling timestamp are pulled from patient_administration to send appointment reminders to all scheduled patients, under the registration/scheduling legitimate use (LU-REG); pseudonymisation is skipped since direct contact details are required for delivery, retention is capped well below the 180-day ceiling with an audited purge on completion, and standard transport/at-rest encryption, access control, notice, audit logging and ROPA accountability apply.

Restricted to the single named patient (mrn-linked records across billing and clinical modules) to reconcile the outstanding invoice with the payer and cross-check charges against the diagnosis; only financial/administrative identifiers, invoice/payer details, and the primary diagnosis were pulled -- no contact or quasi-identifier fields, since they are not needed for this reconciliation task -- under the billing_settlement legitimate-use basis (LU-BILL), with standard transport/at-rest encryption, access control, audited deletion, and no onward use.

Restricted to the single named patient's MRN, pulling only the financial fields needed to reconcile the invoice with the payer (invoice_id, billed_amount, insurance_policy_no, payer_name) and the clinical diagnosis field needed to justify the charges, both linked by MRN; contact/demographic fields were excluded as unnecessary for this billing-reconciliation purpose under data minimisation. Processing rests on the legitimate-use basis LU-BILL (settlement of amounts due), covered by the registration notice NOTICE-REG-2026, retained at the 365-day policy ceiling with scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), transported over TLS and stored encrypted (ENC-REST) behind RBAC (ACL-STORE); pseudonymisation is not applied since direct identifiers (MRN) are required to match records to the payer and policy does not mandate it. The run is logged (AUDIT-LOG), accountable to the DPO, and recorded in the ROPA, with no onward/secondary uses.

Scoped to the single named patient, pulling only the MRN linkage, patient name, diagnosis (to explain the charges), and the financial fields needed to reconcile the invoice with the payer — all within the administrative/financial/direct_identifier categories permitted for billing settlement; pseudonymisation is not applied since the accounts team needs the actual identity to reconcile with the payer, and standard platform safeguards (TLS, encryption at rest, RBAC, audit logging, scheduled purge, DPO accountability, ROPA) are in place under the LU-BILL legitimate-use basis with the 365-day retention ceiling.

Only patient_administration demographic/contact fields (direct_identifier, contact, quasi_identifier categories) are pulled for this single walk-in patient (scope=subject), matching the registration purpose and data minimisation. The job's request to record insurance policy number and coverage details would require administrative_financial fields, which fall under the 'financial' category -- not among the categories the patient_registration policy permits -- so insurance_policy_no and payer_name are excluded despite the job wording; the policy is binding over the request. Admission_ward/admission_datetime were also omitted as unnecessary for a walk-in front-desk registration (no admission event). Retention is set at the 180-day ceiling with PURGE-01 as the deletion mechanism, no onward/secondary uses are declared, lawful basis is legitimate use under LU-REG, and security/accountability controls (TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG, DPO, ROPA, NOTICE-REG-2026) are cited as provided by the deployment. Pseudonymisation on export is not applied since the policy marks it as not required for this purpose.

Only demographic/contact fields from patient_administration needed to register this single walk-in patient are pulled (scope=subject); admission_ward/admission_datetime are excluded as unnecessary for a walk-in front-desk registration (data minimisation). Insurance policy number and payer/coverage fields (administrative_financial/insurance_policy_no, payer_name) are financial-category data not among the categories the patient_registration purpose policy permits (administrative, contact, direct_identifier, quasi_identifier), so despite the job request they are withheld entirely -- policy is binding over task wording. Basis is legitimate use LU-REG (registration/scheduling, the purpose for which data was provided), retention capped at the 180-day ceiling with scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), transport/at-rest encryption and RBAC applied (TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE), pseudonymisation not applied since not required and direct identifiers are needed for front-desk operations, notice NOTICE-REG-2026 covers this purpose and is machine-readable, and the run is audit-logged (AUDIT-LOG) with the DPO accountable and recorded in the ROPA.

Only patient_administration fields needed to identify, contact, and register the walk-in patient are pulled (mrn, name, phone, email, address, DOB, sex, pincode), scoped to this single subject; admission_ward/admission_datetime were excluded as unnecessary for front-desk registration. The requested insurance policy number and coverage details live in administrative_financial and are categorised 'financial', which the patient_registration purpose policy does not permit, so they are omitted despite the job's wording, per data minimisation and the binding category policy. Lawful basis is the recorded legitimate use LU-REG (registration/scheduling), retention is capped at the 180-day policy ceiling with scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), and standard safeguards (TLS, ENC-REST, ACL-STORE, AUDIT-LOG, ROPA, DPO accountability, acknowledged NOTICE-REG-2026) apply; pseudonymisation is not applied since front-desk registration requires real identifiers and the policy does not mandate it.

Scope is restricted to the named patient's records and fields are limited to those needed to produce a diagnosis/medication summary for the ward round (identifying link, ward context, diagnosis, medication, prescribing clinician and encounter time); the job's request to retain a copy for the department's research registry is a distinct secondary use not covered by the care-coordination legitimate-use basis or the purpose policy (onward uses: none), so no research-registry copy is made and secondary_uses is empty.
